Yann LeCun and Randall Balestriero just Proved the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, and found a better way to achieve it. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that AI models trained on different modalities, like images and text, eventually learn similar representations of the world. But this paper shows that how models are trained matters more than simply scaling them up. So they mathematically show that, under certain conditions, two JEPAs trained completely separately can learn essentially the same underlying representation of the world. One learns from different images of the same scene, while the other learns from different descriptions of that scene, without ever being trained on image-text pairs. Their approach achieves the same image-text alignment with 42x fewer training samples than next-token prediction. A 109M-parameter text JEPA even outperforms LLMs up to 72B parameters on cross-modal alignment benchmarks. https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2610.39302

Naval Ravikant once shared a story about Bill Gates shorting Tesla, a bet that could ultimately cost him more than $10 billion. Gates had taken a massive short position against Tesla, reportedly equivalent to roughly 1% of the company’s total shares. Naval suggested that if Tesla became the world’s most valuable company by a wide margin, the losses could be so enormous that even someone as wealthy as Bill Gates could face financial ruin. But what fascinated Naval wasn't the money. It was Elon Musk’s reaction. Musk was genuinely confused. How could someone who publicly championed clean energy financially bet against a company working to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy? To Gates, it was reportedly just a financial decision. But to Musk, it was something much deeper. According to Naval, that moment revealed something fundamental about Elon Musk. Elon Musk is not driven by money, wealth, or status. He is driven by a mission. The billions he earns are not trophies. They are tools.
